in_hebrew.name: אלישיב
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא החיים, ה' הוא החיים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלישיב הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא החיים' או 'ה' הוא החיים'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'אל' או 'אלוהים', שפירושו 'אלוהים', ו'ישיב' שפירושו 'הוא חי' או 'יחיה'. השם אלישיב מופיע בתנ'ך, בספר נחמיה פרק 3 פסוק 1, כשמו של אחד הכוהנים ששימשו בבניית חומות ירושלים.

in_greek.name: Ελισίβ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ελισίβ είναι μια μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος אלישיב, που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ζωή' ή 'Ο Κύριος είναι ζωή'. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος συνδέεται με τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'אל' (Θεός) και 'ישיב' (είναι ζωή). Στην Καινή Διαθήκη δεν υπάρχει άμεση αναφορά στο όνομα αυτό, αλλά η πνευματική σημασία του συνδέεται με την έννοια της ζωής και της σχέσης με το Θεό.

in_latin.name: Elyashiv
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Elyashiv origine hebraicum est, quod significat 'Deus est vita' vel 'Dominus est vita'. Compositum est ex duobus vocabulis: 'אל' (Deus) et 'ישיב' (est vita). In traditione christiana, nomen hoc reflectit ideam vitae aeternae et relationem profundam cum Deo.

in_english.name: Elyashiv
in_english.meaning: God is life or The Lord is life
in_english.long_meaning: The name Elyashiv originates from Hebrew, composed of 'El' (אל) meaning 'God' and 'Yashiv' (ישיב) meaning 'is life' or 'will live'. It appears in the Bible in Nehemiah 3:1, referring to a priest involved in the reconstruction of Jerusalem's walls. The name carries a profound spiritual significance, symbolizing the eternal life and the intimate relationship with God. In Christian tradition, Elyashiv is appreciated for its biblical roots and its expression of faith in God as the source of life.

biblical_reference.note: Elyashiv was a priest who participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eliyahu (Elijah) in Jewish culture is synonymous with prophets and miracles. It is a name of reverence and honor.
data.spiritual_significance: In Jewish spirituality, the name Eliyahu represents connection to the divine, faithfulness, and God's presence in daily life.

historical_references.reference: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the Lubavitcher Rebbe, granted the name Elyashiv to Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Auerbach in 1972, during his tenure as the Rabbi of the Jerusalem Beit Midrash and the Chief Rabbi of Israel.

Rav Chaim Ozer Grodzensky, a prominent Lithuanian Jewish scholar and rabbi, was given the name Elyashiv by his father, Rabbi Yitzchak Elchanan Spektor, in the late 1800s. The name was in honor of Rabbi Eliahu Schapira, who was the Av Beit Din (Head of the Rabbinical Court) of Vilna at the time.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Elyashiv is renowned in Jewish communities, particularly in the context of Modern Orthodox and Haredi Judaism. Elyashiv is the last name of Rabbi Joseph Ber Soloveitchik, a prominent Modern Orthodox rabbi and philosopher, who led the Brisk Yeshiva in Jerusalem. Elyashiv is also the name of Rabbi Yitzchak Elyashiv, a leading Haredi rabbi and former Chief Rabbi of Israel. In the modern context, Elyashiv is a name associated with rabbinic leadership and religious scholarship. It is often mentioned in discussions surrounding Jewish law, philosophy, and education. This name holds significant value in Jewish communities and is frequently referenced on various social media platforms such as Twitter, LinkedIn, and Facebook.
